learningObjectives: Create reusable Java methods with parameters and return values.
Distinguish local variables, parameters, and return values.
Decompose a program into smaller reusable methods.

activities.title: Method Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore each part of a Java method declaration.

content.concept: A Java method can include an access modifier, return type, method name, parameters, and a method body. The return type describes the value returned by the method, or void when no value is returned.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Access modifier that makes the method accessible from other classes where permitted.
Declares the method as belonging to the class rather than an instance.
The return type indicating that the method returns an integer.
The name used when calling the method.
The parameters that receive values supplied by the caller.
Returns the computed result to the caller.

activities.title: Method Call Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the stages of a method call.

content.concept: When a method is called, control transfers to that method. Arguments are matched to parameters, the method body executes, and a return statement can send a value back to the caller.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Parameter and Argument Matcher
activities.instruction: Identify which values are arguments and which are parameters.

content.concept: Parameters are variables declared in a method definition. Arguments are the actual values or expressions supplied when the method is called.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Method Builder
activities.instruction: Build a reusable method that calculates the sum of two integers.

content.concept: Breaking a program into focused methods makes logic easier to reuse, test, read, and maintain. A method should have a clear responsibility and an appropriate interface.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
